title: Supervisor escalation
description: A supervisor escalating a capacity, wellbeing or process problem to the director or state coordinator: what happened, the measures, what has been tried and what is needed. It never describes the content of a contact. Everything is fictional and marked as an exercise product; a real helpline number never appears without the EXERCISE marking, and no real person or address is used.

subtitle.description: Line under the organization: unit, site, period

issue.description: The problem in two or three sentences, with numbers
examples: Texts are waiting 11 minutes and two counselors have asked for a break after back-to-back long contacts.
Moved two supervisors onto text seats.

needed.description: What the supervisor needs and by when
examples: Approve activation of the surge plan and request backup for texts by 20:15.
